report.summary: Analyzed chunk 1 of 5 of daedalus/kairos/gated_writes.py; 13 checkable claims identified; 11 kept, 2 uncheckable.

handoff.purpose: Phase 1 concurrent gating infrastructure: rebasing declared paths, GatedCandidate dataclass, artifact root, relay gate, recording runner, provider receipt, and TaskSpec builder.

symbols.name: _DEFAULT_GATE_TIMEOUT_S
symbols.note: Fallback timeout for curated command gate; mirrors spine.attempt.DEFAULT_GATE_TIMEOUT_S without importing at module scope.

symbols.name: rebase_declared_path
symbols.note: Converts an absolute path under primary_root to repo-relative POSIX string; returns absolute paths outside primary_root unchanged.

symbols.name: rebase_declared_paths
symbols.note: Applies rebase_declared_path to each path in the iterable.

symbols.name: GatedCandidate
symbols.note: Dataclass holding assignment, spec, and result from Phase 1.

symbols.name: _artifact_root_for
symbols.note: Returns path for durable patch storage outside primary checkout.

symbols.name: _relay_gate
symbols.note: Returns a gate callable that judges by offload's own verdict via a mutable box.

symbols.name: _recording_runner
symbols.note: Wraps offload_runner to capture result in a box before gate runs.

symbols.name: _provider_receipt
symbols.note: Projects operational part of offload runner result; never includes prompts or content.

symbols.name: _spec_for
symbols.note: Returns TaskSpec for one assignment (partial implementation visible).

claims.text: This module does not repeat any of that. It has two responsibilities: PHASE 1 -- CONCURRENT GATING (gate_candidates). ... PHASE 2 -- PROMOTION (promote_candidates; opt-in, a separate call, NOT wired into KairosScheduler.dispatch()'s default path)
claims.why: The chunk defines helper functions for Phase 1 and Phase 2 (e.g., _relay_gate, _provider_receipt) but does not include gate_candidates, promote_candidates, or run_write_wave. The claim about wiring into KairosScheduler cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: The primary checkout is untouched -- that is TaskAttempt's own structural guarantee, not something re-implemented or re-verified here.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain the code that runs TaskAttempt or verifies the primary checkout; the claim relies on external module behavior.

claims.text: An absolute path that resolves under primary_root is rebased to its repo-relative form.
claims.why: Lines 72-76: if p.is_absolute() and resolves under primary_root, returns rel.as_posix().

claims.text: An absolute path that resolves OUTSIDE primary_root is returned unchanged.
claims.why: Lines 73-75: try/except ValueError catches the case where relative_to fails, returning raw unchanged.

claims.text: A held candidate cannot live only in AttemptResult.artifact: run_write_wave returns plain dictionaries and TaskAttempt reaps its candidate branch, so those bytes otherwise disappear as soon as the call returns.
claims.why: The function exists to provide a durable external path; the reasoning about disappearance is consistent with the purpose stated.

claims.text: Keep the archive beside the worktree/control state, namespaced by checkout identity, and let TaskAttempt._persist apply its primary-tree fence before it creates or writes anything.
claims.why: The function uses a hash of the repo root to namespace; the reference to TaskAttempt._persist is external but the implementation is consistent with the stated design.

claims.text: A gate callable only ever receives a RunnerContext (worktree/branch/base/task/is_cancelled) -- never the runner's return value -- so there is no direct way to ask 'did offload() call this clean'.
claims.why: The function takes a box dict and returns a _gate closure that reads from box; this is consistent with the claim that the runner's return value is not directly available to the gate.

claims.text: box is a mutable cell the paired runner (_recording_runner) writes its result into before returning; this closure reads it back.
claims.why: Lines 133-134: box['result'] = res in _recording_runner; line 113: res = box.get('result') in _gate.

claims.text: offload can finish with action == 'escalated_after_verify_fail' while wrote is NON-EMPTY, because a write it could not fully roll back is reported in dirty_unreverted and kept in wrote so it stays visible. That leaves a non-empty artifact for a run offload itself considers FAILED, and only checking action == 'offloaded' (not 'artifact exists') refuses it.
claims.why: Line 114: ok = res.get('action') == 'offloaded' and bool(res.get('wrote')). This explicitly checks the action, not just existence of artifact.

claims.text: box['result'] is set the instant the runner returns, which is always BEFORE TaskAttempt calls the gate (see daedalus.spine.attempt.TaskAttempt._run_with_ledger: runner, then artifact capture, then gate) -- so _relay_gate reading box always sees this attempt's own result, never a stale or missing one.
claims.why: Lines 133-134: result is stored immediately after base_runner returns; the gate is called after runner completes per the referenced ordering.

claims.text: The write-wave projection used to drop it, collapsing every provider refusal into 'the runner produced no change to gate'.
claims.why: The function extracts a subset of keys; the docstring describes a past behavior and the current function provides a richer projection.

claims.text: Keep only routing/action facts, measured writes, and rewrite activation/skip provenance -- never prompts, repository content, or arbitrary model prose.
claims.why: Lines 157-170: the function explicitly selects keys like 'provider', 'model', 'action', 'wrote', 'did_work', 'report_status', 'verify', and limited handoff keys; no prompt or content keys are included.

claims.text: This is a deliberate correction (cross-vendor review, Codex, 2026-07-29) to an earlier draft that proposed git apply --check as the sole conflict detector: a check that passes only proves the bytes still match: it does not prove the SEMANTIC content is still correct once an earlier candidate has landed ahead of it.
claims.why: The docstring describes the correction; no code in this chunk contradicts it. The claim is about historical design, not current code behavior.
